title: المتلازمة الإكليلية الحادة وتدبير احتشاء عضلة القلب في الطوارئ
subtitle: Pathophysiology of Myocardial Infarction, Tissue Ischemia, and Reperfusion Protocols
author: هيئة التحرير السريري · WHO UMD

sections.heading: 1. الآلية الفيزيولوجية المرضية لنقص التروية والاحتشاء
paragraphs: Patients presenting to the emergency department with acute retrosternal chest pain and severe Dyspnea require immediate clinical evaluation to rule out Myocardial Infarction. The primary pathophysiological mechanism involves sudden rupture of an atherosclerotic plaque within a coronary artery, leading to acute thrombosis, severe Ischemia, and cellular Hypoxia of the myocardium.

عندما ينقطع التدفق الدموي التاجي لفترة تتجاوز العشرين دقيقة، تبدأ الخلايا العضلية القلبية بالتنخر غير العكوس، مما يؤدي إلى ارتفاع المؤشرات الحيوية القلبية وفي مقدمتها إنزيم Troponin عالي الحساسية، بالتزامن مع تغيرات تخطيطية واضحة.

sections.heading: 2. التظاهرات السريرية واضطرابات النظم المرافقة
paragraphs: During the hyperacute phase of Myocardial Infarction, autonomic nervous system activation frequently triggers sinus Tachycardia or life-threatening ventricular Arrhythmia. If left ventricular systolic function deteriorates rapidly, patients may develop acute Pulmonary Edema and cardiogenic Shock requiring urgent hemodynamic stabilization.

كما يجب الانتباه لدى مرضى السكري وكبار السن لاحتمال حدوث احتشاء صامت يتظاهر فقط بهبوط ضغط الدم الانتصابي (Hypotension) أو ضيق تنفس مفاجئ دون ألم صدري وصفي، وهو ما يستوجب إجراء تخطيط قلب كهربائي خلال أول 10 دقائق من وصول المريض.

sections.heading: 3. إعادة التروية التاجية والتدخل القسطري العاجل
paragraphs: Timely restoration of coronary perfusion via primary percutaneous coronary Angioplasty remains the gold-standard intervention to salvage ischemic myocardium and prevent chronic Cardiomyopathy. Prior to catheterization, dual antiplatelet therapy and anticoagulation are administered unless contraindicated by active Hemorrhage or severe Thrombocytopenia.

title: هندسة الترجمة العصبية المقيدة بالمعجم (GC-NMT) ومنع الهلوسة في النصوص العلمية
subtitle: Combining Transformer Architecture, Deterministic Token Masking, and Vector Embedding
author: فريق أبحاث اللسانيات الحاسوبية

sections.heading: 1. تحدي الهلوسة الدلالية في النماذج اللغوية العامة
paragraphs: Modern Neural Machine Translation systems built upon the Transformer Architecture excel at capturing long-range syntactic dependencies through self-attention mechanisms. However, when translating specialized clinical reports, unconstrained generative models remain vulnerable to semantic Hallucination and inconsistent terminology.
فعلى سبيل المثال، قد تترجم النماذج غير المقيدة المصطلح السريري الواحد بعدة صيغ متباينة في الفقرة ذاتها، أو تخطئ في فك الاختصارات السياقية الحرجة مثل MS وPT، مما يشكل خطراً في التوثيق الطبي والتقني.

sections.heading: 2. التمويه الحتمي للكيانات قبل الترميز (Pre-Tokenization Masking)
paragraphs: To guarantee 100% terminological fidelity without sacrificing grammatical fluency, Glossary-Constrained NMT applies a Deterministic Aho-Corasick scanner prior to subword Tokenization. Verified multi-word terms are replaced with invariant placeholders before passing the sequence into the quantized model.

وبالتوازي مع ذلك، تسمح تقنيات Quantization بتقليص حجم الأوزان الحسابية من 32-bit إلى 8-bit، مما يقلل استهلاك Memory Footprint وزمن الاستجابة Latency ليتم تشغيل المحرك محلياً بالكامل على الهواتف الذكية دون اتصال بالسحابة.

sections.heading: 3. الاسترجاع المعزز بالمعرفة وتحديث الفهارس المتجهة
paragraphs: By combining Vector Embedding similarity with Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Zero-Shot Learning fallbacks, hybrid engines bridge the gap between symbolic lexicography and neural fluency. Even when Fine-Tuning is not feasible on edge devices, dynamic glossary injection ensures immediate adaptation to newly ingested terms.
بفضل هذه البنية الهجينة، يصبح بإمكان المستخدم إضافة أي مصطلح جديد إلى القاموس ليتم اعتماده فوراً في جميع عمليات الترجمة اللاحقة بدقة حتمية.

title: تصميم محركات البحث الفوري SQLite FTS5 والمزامنة المحلية في بيئة Termux
subtitle: High-Concurrency Edge Storage, Idempotency, and Sub-Millisecond Full-Text Search
author: قسم هندسة البرمجيات المدمجة

sections.heading: 1. الفهرسة المعكوسة (Inverted Indexing) في SQLite FTS5
paragraphs: Building an offline-first knowledge graph capable of searching tens of thousands of bilingual records with ultra-low Latency requires an inverted index structure. SQLite FTS5 tokenizes both Arabic and English strings into prefix trees, enabling instant Concordance lookup across definitions and contextual examples.

وعند تفعيل وضع الكتابة المسبقة في السجل (Write-Ahead Logging - WAL)، تتحقق درجة عالية من Concurrency تسمح لسكربتات بايثون في Termux بضخ المصطلحات الجديدة في الوقت نفسه الذي يتصفح فيه المستخدم الواجهة دون أي قفل لقاعدة البيانات.

sections.heading: 2. ضمان عدم التكرار (Idempotency) وسلامة التسلسل البياني
paragraphs: Every batch ingestion pipeline must enforce strict Idempotency and schema validation during JSON Serialization. Using a Deterministic merge policy ensures that importing updated lexicon files enriches existing entries with new contextual sentences rather than duplicating records.
كما تساعد الخوارزميات الاستدلالية (Heuristic) في اكتشاف الروابط الثنائية تلقائياً بين المصطلحات المشتركة في الجمل، مما يحول القاموس من قائمة جامدة إلى شبكة معرفية حية.

author: وحدة التراث العلمي وتاريخ الطب

sections.heading: 1. مدرسة الترجمة العباسية وتأسيس المصطلح السريري الدقيق
paragraphs: شهدت الحضارة العربية الإسلامية في القرنين الثالث والرابع للهجرة نهضة علمية غير مسبوقة في تعريب وتأصيل المصطلحات الطبية والفلسفية. وقد اعتمد العلماء والأطباء مثل حنين بن إسحاق وأبو بكر الرازي وابن سينا منهجية علمية صارمة تقوم على الاشتقاق الصرفي والنحت الدلالي لترجمة الجذور اليونانية واللاتينية إلى مقابلات عربية فصيحة ودقيقة.

Classical Arabic medical encyclopedias systematically documented complex clinical conditions such as Pneumonia, Meningitis, Hemorrhage, and Jaundice (Hyperbilirubinemia) centuries before modern European nosology standardized clinical classifications.

title: مدخل إلى علم الدم وتكوّن خلايا الدم
subtitle: Introduction to Hematology and Hematopoiesis
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. مكونات الدم ووظائفها
paragraphs: Blood consists of plasma and formed elements. Plasma carries water, electrolytes, nutrients, hormones, and plasma proteins; formed elements include erythrocytes (RBCs), leukocytes (WBCs), and platelets. اربط كل عنصر بوظيفته: RBCs لنقل الغازات، WBCs للدفاع المناعي، والصفائح مع عوامل التخثر لإيقاف النزف.

sections.heading: 2. Hematopoiesis ومواقعها
paragraphs: Hematopoiesis is the continuous production of blood cells from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). During fetal life, the major sites change from yolk sac to liver and then bone marrow. After birth, active marrow is progressively concentrated in the axial skeleton, especially vertebrae, sternum, ribs, and pelvis. Extramedullary hematopoiesis means blood-cell production outside marrow, classically in liver or spleen when marrow demand is high or marrow function is impaired.

sections.heading: 3. تنظيم تكوّن الخلايا
paragraphs: HSCs differentiate into myeloid and lymphoid lineages. Erythropoietin (EPO), produced mainly by the kidneys in response to tissue hypoxia, stimulates erythroid production. Thrombopoietin supports megakaryocyte and platelet production; colony-stimulating factors regulate granulocyte and monocyte lineages. Iron, vitamin B12, folate, protein, and healthy marrow stroma are essential.

sections.heading: 4. نقاط امتحانية
paragraphs: Remember: EPO → kidney; HSC → all blood-cell lineages; extramedullary hematopoiesis → outside bone marrow. The classic fetal sequence is yolk sac → liver (major fetal site) → bone marrow. Do not confuse the site of maturation of T lymphocytes (thymus) with the site of production of their precursors (bone marrow).

title: قراءة CBC ومؤشرات كريات الدم الحمراء
subtitle: Complete Blood Count, RBC Indices, and Peripheral Smear
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. قراءة CBC بطريقة منظمة
paragraphs: Start with hemoglobin (Hb) and hematocrit (Hct) to assess anemia, then RBC count and red-cell indices. Review WBC count with differential, and platelet count. Always interpret values using age-, sex-, pregnancy-, and laboratory-specific reference ranges; a single numerical range is not universal.

sections.heading: 2. أهم RBC indices
paragraphs: MCV (mean corpuscular volume) describes average RBC size: microcytic, normocytic, or macrocytic. MCH (mean corpuscular hemoglobin) is the average amount of hemoglobin per RBC, while MCHC (mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration) reflects hemoglobin concentration within packed RBCs. RDW measures variation in RBC size (anisocytosis). Low MCV and low MCH are common in iron deficiency and thalassemia; increased MCV suggests macrocytosis.

sections.heading: 3. Peripheral blood smear
paragraphs: A smear adds morphology that automated indices cannot fully describe. Microcytes are small cells; hypochromia means increased central pallor; target cells may occur in thalassemia and liver disease; spherocytes occur in hereditary spherocytosis or immune hemolysis; schistocytes suggest mechanical fragmentation; sickle cells indicate HbS-related disease. Reticulocytes indicate marrow response.

sections.heading: 4. كيف تقترب من سؤال الحالة؟
paragraphs: First classify anemia by MCV. Then inspect reticulocyte count: a low/inappropriately normal count suggests reduced production; a high count suggests blood loss or hemolysis if marrow response is intact. Next use ferritin, iron studies, bilirubin, LDH, haptoglobin, and smear according to the suspected mechanism. MCQ trap: MCH is an amount per cell; MCHC is a concentration.

sections.heading: 5. Quick check
paragraphs: A patient has low Hb, low MCV, low MCH, and high RDW: iron deficiency is likely, but confirm with iron studies. A patient has low MCV with a relatively preserved/high RBC count and normal iron stores: consider thalassemia trait.

title: تصنيف فقر الدم وخوارزمية التشخيص
subtitle: Anemia: Classification and Diagnostic Approach
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. تعريف وآليات Anemia
paragraphs: Anemia is a reduction in hemoglobin concentration below the appropriate reference range for age and sex. The three broad mechanisms are decreased RBC production, increased RBC destruction (hemolysis), and blood loss. These mechanisms guide the differential diagnosis more reliably than memorizing long lists in isolation.

sections.heading: 2. التصنيف حسب MCV
paragraphs: Microcytic anemia: iron deficiency, thalassemia, and some anemia of inflammation or sideroblastic disorders. Normocytic anemia: acute blood loss, hemolysis, chronic kidney disease, early iron deficiency, or marrow failure. Macrocytic anemia: vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol/liver disease, hypothyroidism, medications, and marrow disorders. Macrocytosis is not synonymous with megaloblastic anemia.

sections.heading: 3. Reticulocyte count يحدد استجابة النخاع
paragraphs: Reticulocytes are young RBCs recently released from marrow. A high reticulocyte response supports hemolysis or blood loss; a low response suggests inadequate production. Interpret the count in context of anemia severity and, clinically, use a corrected reticulocyte index when appropriate.

sections.heading: 4. خطة حل الحالة
paragraphs: Step 1: confirm low Hb using the correct reference range. Step 2: classify by MCV. Step 3: assess reticulocyte response. Step 4: use smear and targeted tests (ferritin/iron profile, B12/folate, renal function, hemolysis markers, or marrow studies). Step 5: identify the cause, not just the anemia label. A common exam error is diagnosing IDA from microcytosis alone without checking iron status.

sections.heading: 5. High-yield distinction
paragraphs: Low reticulocytes + pancytopenia raises concern for marrow failure or infiltration. High reticulocytes + raised unconjugated bilirubin supports hemolysis. Microcytosis with low ferritin strongly supports iron deficiency.

title: فقر الدم بعوز الحديد
subtitle: Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA)
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. Iron absorption and regulation
paragraphs: Iron is absorbed mainly in the duodenum and proximal jejunum. Non-heme iron absorption is enhanced by vitamin C and reduced by substances such as tea tannins. DMT1 transports ferrous iron (Fe2+) into enterocytes; ferritin stores iron; ferroportin exports it; transferrin transports circulating iron. Hepcidin, produced by the liver, inhibits ferroportin and reduces intestinal iron absorption and iron release from stores.

sections.heading: 2. Causes and clinical manifestations
paragraphs: Common causes include inadequate intake, increased requirements during growth, malabsorption, and chronic blood loss. Findings may include pallor, fatigue, poor concentration, pica, glossitis, koilonychia, and tachycardia. Symptoms depend on severity and chronicity; absence of classic signs does not exclude IDA.

sections.heading: 3. Laboratory pattern
paragraphs: Typical IDA: low Hb, low MCV, low MCH, low serum iron, low ferritin, increased TIBC, and reduced transferrin saturation. The smear is often microcytic and hypochromic, sometimes with anisopoikilocytosis. Important trap: ferritin is an acute-phase reactant and may be normal or elevated during inflammation despite depleted iron stores.

sections.heading: 4. Treatment principles
paragraphs: Treat the underlying cause and replace iron according to the applicable age-specific guideline. Oral iron is commonly first-line when absorption and tolerance are adequate; parenteral iron is reserved for selected situations. Transfusion is not routine treatment for uncomplicated IDA and is reserved for selected severe or unstable cases. Follow-up should demonstrate a hematologic response and eventual replenishment of stores.

sections.heading: 5. IDA exam clues
paragraphs: Low ferritin + high TIBC = classic iron deficiency pattern. Main absorption site = duodenum/proximal jejunum. Vitamin C increases non-heme iron absorption. Tea may reduce absorption. Never equate every microcytic anemia with IDA.

title: الثلاسيميا واضطرابات الهيموغلوبين
subtitle: Thalassemia and Hemoglobinopathies
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. أساسيات Hemoglobin
paragraphs: Adult HbA is composed of two alpha and two beta chains (α2β2). Thalassemia is a quantitative defect: reduced or absent globin-chain synthesis. This differs from many structural hemoglobin variants, in which the globin chain is produced but has an altered amino-acid sequence.

sections.heading: 2. Beta-thalassemia
paragraphs: Reduced beta-chain synthesis causes excess unmatched alpha chains, ineffective erythropoiesis, and hemolysis. Beta-thalassemia major often becomes clinically apparent after fetal hemoglobin (HbF) declines in infancy. Severe anemia, growth failure, hepatosplenomegaly, marrow expansion, and skeletal changes may occur. Hemoglobin analysis typically shows markedly increased HbF; HbA may be very low or absent in severe disease.

sections.heading: 3. Alpha-thalassemia gene dosage
paragraphs: Humans normally have four alpha-globin genes. One affected gene: silent carrier; two: alpha-thalassemia trait; three: HbH disease (β4 tetramers); four: Hb Bart's (γ4 tetramers), associated with severe fetal disease. Alpha-thalassemia trait can resemble IDA on CBC because both can cause microcytosis, so iron studies and hemoglobin analysis/genetic testing may be needed.

sections.heading: 4. مقارنة IDA وThalassemia trait
paragraphs: Both may show low MCV and MCH. IDA usually has low ferritin and often increased RDW; thalassemia trait commonly has normal iron stores and a relatively preserved or increased RBC count. These are clues, not absolute rules. Do not prescribe iron for thalassemia unless iron deficiency is also demonstrated.

sections.heading: 5. Complications and management concepts
paragraphs: Transfusion-dependent thalassemia may require regular RBC transfusions and iron chelation to prevent iron overload in the heart, liver, and endocrine organs. Selected patients may be candidates for hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation. The treatment plan is specialist-led and depends on genotype, severity, and complications.

title: فقر الدم المنجلي والأزمات الحادة
subtitle: Sickle Cell Disease and Acute Crises
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. Molecular pathophysiology
paragraphs: Sickle cell disease results from a beta-globin mutation in which glutamic acid is replaced by valine at position 6, producing HbS. When deoxygenated, HbS polymerizes; RBCs become rigid and sickle-shaped. Repeated sickling causes chronic hemolysis, vaso-occlusion, ischemia, and progressive organ injury.

sections.heading: 2. Triggers and manifestations
paragraphs: Hypoxia, dehydration, infection, cold exposure, and physiologic stress can promote sickling. Clinical features include chronic hemolytic anemia, jaundice, painful vaso-occlusive episodes, dactylitis in infants, acute chest syndrome, stroke, avascular necrosis, pigment gallstones, and renal concentrating defects. Repeated splenic infarction can lead to functional asplenia.

sections.heading: 3. التفريق بين الأزمات
paragraphs: Hemolytic crisis: increased RBC destruction, usually with increased reticulocytes. Aplastic crisis, classically due to Parvovirus B19: sudden fall in Hb with markedly reduced reticulocytes. Sequestration crisis: sudden pooling of blood in spleen or liver, acute organ enlargement, severe anemia, and possible shock; reticulocytes are often increased. The reticulocyte count is a key discriminator.

sections.heading: 4. Infection risk and prevention
paragraphs: Functional asplenia increases susceptibility to encapsulated bacteria, especially Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae type b. Prevention includes recommended vaccination, penicillin prophylaxis in appropriate children, hydration, and prompt assessment of fever. Hydroxyurea increases HbF and reduces vaso-occlusive complications; monitoring is required because myelosuppression can occur.

sections.heading: 5. Exam clues
paragraphs: HbS polymerizes when deoxygenated. Aplastic crisis → Parvovirus B19 + low reticulocytes. Functional asplenia → encapsulated organisms. Hydroxyurea → increased HbF. Acute chest syndrome and stroke are serious complications requiring urgent specialist management.

title: فقر الدم ضخم الأرومات ونقص B12 والفولات
subtitle: Megaloblastic Anemia: Vitamin B12 and Folate
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. Mechanism and morphology
paragraphs: Megaloblastic anemia results from impaired DNA synthesis, most commonly due to vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. Nuclear maturation lags behind cytoplasmic maturation, producing macro-ovalocytes in blood and nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony in marrow. Hypersegmented neutrophils are a classic peripheral smear clue; giant metamyelocytes may be seen in marrow.

sections.heading: 2. Folate versus Vitamin B12
paragraphs: Folate is absorbed mainly in the proximal small intestine. Vitamin B12 binds intrinsic factor and is absorbed in the terminal ileum. Folate deficiency may result from poor intake, malabsorption, increased demand, or certain medications. B12 deficiency may result from inadequate intake, intrinsic-factor problems, or terminal ileal disease/resection.

sections.heading: 3. Neurological distinction
paragraphs: Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy and other neurologic abnormalities; isolated folate deficiency does not typically produce the same neurologic syndrome. Both can cause macrocytosis and megaloblastic blood-film changes.

sections.heading: 4. Clinical safety point
paragraphs: Replace the deficient vitamin and treat the underlying cause. Do not give folic acid alone when B12 deficiency is possible: the anemia may improve while B12-related neurological injury continues. Reticulocytosis after effective replacement is an expected marrow response.

sections.heading: 5. MCQ anchors
paragraphs: B12 absorption → intrinsic factor + terminal ileum. Folate absorption → proximal small intestine. Hypersegmented neutrophils → megaloblastic anemia. Neurologic manifestations → think B12 deficiency.

title: فقر الدم الانحلالي والاختبارات المخبرية
subtitle: Hemolytic Anemia and Hemolysis Workup
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. Definition and classification
paragraphs: Hemolytic anemia occurs when RBC destruction exceeds marrow replacement. Normal RBC lifespan is approximately 120 days. Hemolysis may be intravascular (within blood vessels) or extravascular (mainly macrophages in spleen and liver). Causes may be intrinsic to RBCs (membrane, enzyme, hemoglobin defects) or extrinsic (immune, infection, drugs, or mechanical injury).

sections.heading: 2. Laboratory pattern
paragraphs: Typical findings include increased reticulocytes, increased unconjugated bilirubin, increased LDH, and reduced haptoglobin; urine findings depend on whether intravascular hemolysis is present. The blood film may show polychromasia and characteristic abnormal forms. A direct antiglobulin test (DAT/Direct Coombs) supports immune-mediated hemolysis when positive, but must be interpreted with the clinical picture.

sections.heading: 3. Intravascular versus extravascular
paragraphs: Intravascular hemolysis may cause hemoglobinemia, hemoglobinuria, and marked haptoglobin consumption. Extravascular hemolysis is mediated by macrophages in spleen/liver and may cause splenomegaly and jaundice. These patterns overlap; do not treat one laboratory marker as diagnostic alone.

sections.heading: 4. Important causes
paragraphs: Intrinsic causes include hereditary spherocytosis, G6PD deficiency, pyruvate kinase deficiency, sickle cell disease, and thalassemia. Extrinsic causes include autoimmune hemolytic anemia, infections, drugs, and microangiopathic processes. The smear and targeted tests help identify the mechanism.

sections.heading: 5. MCQ reasoning
paragraphs: High reticulocytes + high unconjugated bilirubin supports hemolysis. Low reticulocytes in an acutely anemic patient suggests impaired production or aplastic crisis rather than a typical compensatory hemolytic response. DAT positivity points toward immune-mediated destruction.

title: فشل نخاع العظم وقلة خلايا الدم الشاملة
subtitle: Bone Marrow Failure, Aplastic Anemia, and Pancytopenia
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. Definitions
paragraphs: Pancytopenia means reduction in all three major blood-cell lines: RBCs, WBCs, and platelets. Aplastic anemia is a bone-marrow failure syndrome commonly producing pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow. Pure red cell aplasia selectively reduces erythroid precursors, causing anemia and reticulocytopenia while other lineages may be relatively preserved.

sections.heading: 2. Causes and clues
paragraphs: Acquired marrow suppression may follow drugs, toxins, radiation, infections, or immune-mediated injury; some cases are idiopathic. Inherited marrow-failure syndromes include Fanconi anemia and other congenital disorders, sometimes associated with physical abnormalities. Parvovirus B19 can transiently suppress erythropoiesis and precipitate aplastic crisis, especially in chronic hemolytic disease.

sections.heading: 3. Diagnostic approach
paragraphs: Repeat CBC and peripheral smear, review medications/exposures and infection history, assess reticulocytes, and investigate nutritional, infectious, immune, and marrow causes. Bone marrow examination may be required. Pancytopenia is a finding, not a final diagnosis.

sections.heading: 4. Differentiating pure red cell aplasia
paragraphs: Pure red cell aplasia typically presents with anemia and very low reticulocytes, with markedly reduced erythroid precursors in marrow. In uncomplicated non-immune aplasia, bilirubin is not expected to rise from hemolysis. Compare this with hemolytic anemia, where reticulocytes usually rise if marrow reserve is adequate.

sections.heading: 5. Exam anchors
paragraphs: Pancytopenia = low RBCs + WBCs + platelets. Aplastic anemia = marrow failure and hypocellularity. Pure red cell aplasia = selective erythroid precursor loss + low reticulocytes.

title: كريات الدم البيضاء والمناعة والتفريق العددي
subtitle: Leukocytes, Differential Count, and Immune Functions
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. Leukocyte overview
paragraphs: Leukocytes protect against infection and participate in inflammation and adaptive immunity. The main circulating types are neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils. Differential count reports the proportion or absolute number of each type; absolute counts are often more clinically informative than percentages alone.

sections.heading: 2. Granulocytes
paragraphs: Neutrophils are usually the most abundant circulating leukocytes and are central to acute bacterial defense and phagocytosis. Eosinophils participate in responses to helminths and allergic disease; their granules contain major basic protein. Basophils contain histamine and heparin and participate in IgE-associated immediate hypersensitivity.

sections.heading: 3. Monocytes and lymphocytes
paragraphs: Monocytes circulate in blood and can differentiate into macrophages in tissues. Tissue-specific macrophages include Kupffer cells in liver, microglia in CNS, and osteoclasts in bone. B lymphocytes can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells; T lymphocytes mediate cellular immunity and mature in the thymus.

sections.heading: 4. WBC count patterns
paragraphs: Neutrophilia may occur in bacterial infection, inflammation, stress, or corticosteroid exposure. Neutropenia may occur with viral infections, drugs, marrow suppression, or severe sepsis. Eosinophilia suggests parasitic infection or allergic/drug-related disease in the right context. A left shift means increased immature neutrophil forms, especially band cells.

sections.heading: 5. Exam clues
paragraphs: Most abundant WBC → neutrophil. Helminth defense → eosinophil/major basic protein. Histamine → basophil/mast-cell pathway. Monocyte in tissue → macrophage. Left shift → increased immature neutrophils.

title: اللوكيميا الحادة والمزمنة ومبادئ التشخيص
subtitle: Leukemia: Acute and Chronic Patterns
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. Definition and classification
paragraphs: Leukemia is a clonal malignant proliferation of hematopoietic cells involving bone marrow and often peripheral blood. Broad classification is myeloid versus lymphoid, and acute versus chronic. Acute leukemias are characterized by accumulation of immature blasts and typically present rapidly; chronic leukemias often involve more mature-appearing cells and may evolve more slowly.

sections.heading: 2. Acute leukemia
paragraphs: Acute leukemia replaces normal marrow, causing anemia, thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia or dysfunctional leukocytes. Common clinical manifestations include fatigue/pallor, infections/fever, bruising/bleeding, bone pain, and sometimes organ infiltration. Diagnosis requires blood and marrow evaluation with morphology, immunophenotyping, cytogenetic, and molecular studies.

sections.heading: 3. AML versus ALL
paragraphs: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) arises from myeloid precursors; acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) arises from lymphoid precursors and is common in childhood. Myeloperoxidase positivity supports myeloid lineage; lymphoid lineage is established by immunophenotypic markers. Do not diagnose lineage from age or one symptom alone.

sections.heading: 4. Chronic leukemia concepts
paragraphs: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is associated with the BCR::ABL1 fusion (Philadelphia chromosome) and proliferation of granulocytic cells. In chronic phase, cells may be relatively mature; progression to accelerated/blast phase produces more immature and dysfunctional cells. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) involves clonal mature B lymphocytes and is usually a disease of older adults.

sections.heading: 5. Exam reasoning
paragraphs: Blasts + marrow failure symptoms suggest acute leukemia. Auer rods and MPO support AML. BCR::ABL1/Philadelphia chromosome suggests CML. ALL is a major childhood acute leukemia. A high WBC count does not guarantee effective immunity; leukemic cells may be functionally defective.

title: الإرقاء والتخثر والصفائح الدموية
subtitle: Hemostasis, Platelets, and Coagulation
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. Primary hemostasis
paragraphs: Vascular injury causes vasoconstriction and exposes subendothelial collagen. Platelets adhere through von Willebrand factor (vWF) and platelet GPIb, become activated, and aggregate through GPIIb/IIIa binding fibrinogen. This forms the initial platelet plug. Disorders of platelet number or function commonly cause mucocutaneous bleeding.

sections.heading: 2. Secondary hemostasis
paragraphs: Coagulation factors generate thrombin, which converts fibrinogen to fibrin. Fibrin stabilizes the platelet plug. The intrinsic and extrinsic pathways converge on factor X and the common pathway. PT/INR assesses the extrinsic/common pathway (especially factor VII and common factors); aPTT assesses intrinsic/common pathway factors. Interpret tests with medication and clinical context.

sections.heading: 3. Platelets and clinical patterns
paragraphs: Thrombocytopenia or platelet dysfunction often causes petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gum bleeding, or heavy menstrual bleeding. Coagulation-factor deficiencies more often cause deep tissue bleeding, hemarthrosis, or delayed bleeding. These are useful patterns, not absolute rules.

sections.heading: 4. Fibrinolysis and DIC
paragraphs: Plasmin breaks down fibrin during fibrinolysis; D-dimer reflects breakdown of cross-linked fibrin. Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) is systemic activation of coagulation with consumption of platelets and factors, causing both thrombosis and bleeding. Typical tests may show low platelets, prolonged PT/aPTT, low fibrinogen, and elevated D-dimer, depending on timing and cause.

sections.heading: 5. High-yield comparisons
paragraphs: vWF: platelet adhesion; GPIIb/IIIa: platelet aggregation; thrombin: fibrinogen → fibrin; plasmin: fibrin breakdown. PT/INR: extrinsic/common. aPTT: intrinsic/common. DIC: consumption coagulopathy with simultaneous clotting and bleeding.

title: فصائل الدم ونقل الدم والأنسجة اللمفاوية
subtitle: ABO/Rh Blood Groups, Transfusion, and Lymphoid Histology
author: UMEDT Study Series · Hematology

sections.heading: 1. ABO and Rh basics
paragraphs: ABO blood groups depend on A and/or B antigens on RBC membranes and naturally occurring plasma antibodies. Group A has A antigen and anti-B; group B has B antigen and anti-A; group AB has both antigens and neither anti-A nor anti-B; group O has neither antigen and has both antibodies. RhD status depends on the D antigen; anti-D is generally an immune antibody formed after exposure.

sections.heading: 2. Transfusion safety
paragraphs: ABO-incompatible RBC transfusion can cause severe acute intravascular hemolysis. Compatibility testing includes blood grouping, antibody screening, and crossmatching according to clinical policy. Emergency transfusion decisions follow local protocols and must account for pregnancy, prior antibodies, and component type; do not rely on simplified universal-donor slogans without context.

sections.heading: 3. Primary and secondary lymphoid organs
paragraphs: Primary lymphoid organs are sites of lymphocyte development/maturation: bone marrow for B-cell development and thymus for T-cell maturation. Secondary lymphoid organs include lymph nodes, spleen, and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT), where immune responses are initiated.

sections.heading: 4. Histology: lymph node, spleen, thymus
paragraphs: Lymph node: cortex contains B-cell follicles; paracortex is T-cell rich; medulla contains cords and sinuses. Spleen: white pulp is lymphoid tissue around central arterioles; PALS is T-cell rich; red pulp contains splenic cords (cords of Billroth) and sinusoids and filters blood. Thymus has cortex and medulla; Hassall corpuscles are characteristic of the medulla, and the thymus is not organized into typical lymphoid follicles.

sections.heading: 5. MALT and Peyer's patches
paragraphs: MALT is lymphoid tissue associated with mucosal surfaces. GALT is in the gastrointestinal tract, BALT in the respiratory tract. Peyer's patches are aggregated lymphoid nodules in the ileum. Lymph follicles may be primary or secondary; a secondary follicle has a germinal center.

sections.heading: 6. Histology MCQ anchors
paragraphs: T-cell maturation → thymus. T-cell zone of spleen → PALS. Spleen red pulp → cords of Billroth and sinusoids. Hassall corpuscles → thymic medulla. Peyer's patches → ileum. GALT → gastrointestinal mucosa.

title: أساسيات علم الطفيليات وتصنيف الديدان وطرق الانتقال
subtitle: General Concepts • Classification • Hosts • Transmission
author: UMEDT — Parasitology Practical Course

sections.heading: 1. Core definitions — احفظ التعريف الإنجليزي كما هو
paragraphs: Endoparasites: parasites that live inside the body of their host. أمثلة المقرر: Ascaris lumbricoides, Ancylostoma, Entamoeba histolytica.
Ectoparasites: parasites that live on the outer surface of their host. أمثلة: Fleas, lice (Pediculus), ticks and mites.
Obligate parasites: cannot live or reproduce without their host؛ تعتمد كلياً على العائل. أمثلة تعليمية في المقرر: Plasmodium وTrichinella spiralis.
Facultative parasites: normally free-living or non-parasitic organisms that may become parasitic under certain conditions. مثال مذكور: Acanthamoeba spp.

Accidental parasites: infect an unusual or unnatural host rather than their usual natural host. Temporary parasites: contact the host only for feeding, then leave. Opportunistic parasites: cause disease particularly when host defenses are impaired (immunocompromised host).

sections.heading: 2. Routes of transmission — اربط الطريق بالمثال
paragraphs: Direct transmission: انتقال مباشر من شخص إلى آخر بالتلامس أو انتقال الطور المعدي مباشرة.
Vertical transmission: mother-to-child transmission during pregnancy or delivery.
Indirect transmission: عبر وسيط غير حي مثل contaminated food, water, soil أو عبر Vector.
Percutaneous transmission: دخول الطفيل باختراق الجلد مباشرة؛ المثال الأهم في هذا المقرر Schistosoma cercariae، وكذلك filariform L3 of Strongyloides.
تمييز مهم: Vector كائن حي ينقل العامل الممرض؛ أما contaminated water/food/soil فهي vehicles أو مصادر انتقال غير حية.

sections.heading: 3. Helminths taxonomy — خريطة التصنيف
paragraphs: Helminths in this guide are grouped into two major phyla: Nemathelminthes / Nematoda (roundworms) and Platyhelminthes (flatworms).
Nematoda: Intestinal nematodes مثل Ascaris, Trichuris, Enterobius, Strongyloides؛ وBlood/Tissue nematodes مثل Loa loa.
Platyhelminthes: Class Cestoda (tapeworms) وتشمل Taenia, Hymenolepis, Diphyllobothrium, Echinococcus؛ وClass Trematoda (flukes) وتشمل Fasciola, Schistosoma, Heterophyes.
Spelling correction: الصحيح Trematoda وflukes، وليس flucks. احفظ التصنيف كما يرد في محاضرتك إذا كان الدكتور يستخدم تسمية أقدم.

sections.heading: 4. Practical learning map — ماذا تتعرف عليه في الشريحة؟
paragraphs: لكل parasite درّب نفسك على ستة مفاتيح: (1) الاسم العلمي، (2) common name، (3) habitat، (4) infective stage / mode of infection، (5) diagnostic stage and specimen، (6) distinctive morphology.
لا تخلط بين Infective stage الذي يدخل الإنسان وبين Diagnostic stage الذي نبحث عنه في العينة. مثال: Strongyloides infective stage = filariform L3؛ أما الشائع في stool diagnosis فهو rhabditiform larva.
في أسئلة الصور ابدأ بالشكل العام ثم العلامة الفارقة: spine, polar plugs, operculum, polar filaments, rostellum/hooks, uterine branches.

title: الديدان الأسطوانية المعوية — Nematodes Diagnostic Atlas
subtitle: Ascaris • Trichuris • Enterobius • Strongyloides
author: UMEDT — Parasitology Practical Course

sections.heading: 1. Ascaris lumbricoides — Roundworm
paragraphs: Habitat: small intestine. Mode of infection: ingestion of embryonated eggs in contaminated food/water. The infective egg is embryonated; eggs are passed in stool and mature in soil.
Adult morphology: female is larger with a relatively straight posterior end; male is smaller with a curved/coiled posterior end. The anterior end has three lips.

Egg identification: fertilized egg is rounded/oval with a thick shell and mammillated outer coat; unfertilized egg is longer, larger, and has irregular mammillations with granular contents. Decorticated eggs have lost the outer mammillated coat.

Practical spotter: distinguish male vs female by posterior end; distinguish fertilized vs unfertilized egg by shape, shell and contents. Diagnostic specimen is stool for eggs; adult worms may occasionally be passed.

sections.heading: 2. Trichuris trichiura — Whipworm
paragraphs: Habitat: large intestine, especially caecum and appendix. Infection follows ingestion of embryonated eggs from contaminated food or water.
Adult morphology: whip-shaped worm; long thin anterior portion and thicker posterior portion. Female posterior end is straight; male posterior end is coiled.
Diagnostic egg: barrel/lemon-shaped, thick shell, with two bipolar plugs (polar plugs) — one at each pole. This is the most important image-recognition clue.
Common name mnemonic: Whipworm → whip-like body; bipolar plugs → Trichuris egg.

sections.heading: 3. Enterobius vermicularis — Pinworm
paragraphs: Habitat: caecum, appendix and ascending colon. Transmission: ingestion of infective eggs from contaminated fingers/surfaces; autoinfection may occur, and retroinfection is described in the course.
Adult female: relatively long, slender body with a long pointed posterior tail; male is smaller with a blunt/coiled posterior end.
Egg: asymmetrical, planoconvex / D-shaped (one side flattened), usually identified by the perianal cellophane-tape test rather than routine stool examination.
Course treatment list: Mebendazole or Piperazine. Use the prescribed lecture reference for exam recall; actual treatment depends on current clinical guidance and patient context.

sections.heading: 4. Strongyloides stercoralis — Threadworm
paragraphs: Habitat: parasitic adult females live in the small intestine, particularly duodenum and jejunum. Infective stage: filariform larva (L3), which penetrates the skin.
Diagnostic clue: rhabditiform larva is commonly detected in stool. Its rhabditoid esophagus has a short anterior corpus, a postmedian constriction (isthmus), and a posterior bulb.

Do not confuse the two larval forms: Rhabditiform = diagnostic in stool; Filariform L3 = infective and skin-penetrating. Autoinfection can maintain infection and may lead to hyperinfection in immunosuppressed patients.

The supplied guide lists thiabendazole and ivermectin; ivermectin is generally the preferred treatment in current clinical references. Drug choice/dose is outside this practical identification lesson.

sections.heading: 5. Rapid comparison — intestinal nematodes
paragraphs: Ascaris: embryonated egg ingestion; small intestine; fertilized egg thick/mammillated; unfertilized egg elongated.
Trichuris: embryonated egg ingestion; caecum/appendix; barrel-shaped egg with bipolar plugs; adult whip-shaped.
Enterobius: hand-to-mouth egg ingestion; caecum/colon; D-shaped egg; perianal tape test; pointed female tail.
Strongyloides: skin penetration by L3; duodenum/jejunum; rhabditiform larva in stool; prominent rhabditoid esophagus; autoinfection.
Memory key: Ascaris = mammillated; Trichuris = two plugs; Enterobius = one flat side; Strongyloides = larva in stool.

title: الديدان الخيطية والأنسجة — Loa loa
subtitle: Subcutaneous Filarial Worms • Microfilaria • Vector
author: UMEDT — Parasitology Practical Course

sections.heading: 1. Loa loa — African eye worm
paragraphs: Habitat: subcutaneous tissue; adult worm may migrate across the subconjunctiva. Common name: African eye worm.
Vector: Chrysops fly (day-biting deer fly). Infective stage: third-stage filariform larva (L3) transmitted during the bite and entering through the wound.

Adult female is longer than the male. The course sheet describes female around 2–2.5 cm and male around 1–1.5 cm; CDC DPDx gives larger adult measurements, so prioritize the exact range printed in the practical guide for its spotter question.

Diagnostic morphology: sheathed microfilaria in peripheral blood film; nuclei extend all the way to the tip of the tail. Microfilariae show diurnal periodicity, so blood collection is best around midday (approximately 10 AM–2 PM).

sections.heading: 2. Practical identification checklist
paragraphs: If the image is a blood smear containing a sheathed microfilaria with nuclei reaching the tail tip, think Loa loa.
If the question mentions an African eye worm, Calabar swelling, or a Chrysops bite, the intended answer is Loa loa.
Do not confuse the adult habitat with the diagnostic specimen: adults are subcutaneous; microfilariae are identified in peripheral blood.

title: الديدان الشريطية — Cestodes Diagnostic Atlas
subtitle: Taenia solium • Taenia saginata • Hymenolepis nana • Diphyllobothrium • Echinococcus
author: UMEDT — Parasitology Practical Course

sections.heading: 1. Taenia solium — Pork tapeworm
paragraphs: Habitat: small intestine, mainly jejunum and ileum. Human intestinal taeniasis follows ingestion of undercooked pork containing cysticerci. Important distinction: ingestion of T. solium eggs can cause cysticercosis; ingestion of cysticerci in pork causes intestinal taeniasis.

Scolex: globular, four suckers, armed rostellum with two rows of hooks. Adult has lateral genital pore. Taenia egg is spherical with a radially striated embryophore and a hexacanth embryo (six hooklets).

Gravid proglottid: central uterine stem with about 7–13 primary lateral branches. T. saginata usually has 12–30. The ranges overlap at 12–13, so count branches rather than relying on a strict <12 / >12 rule.
Cysticercus cellulosae: fluid-filled thin-walled cyst with an invaginated scolex, suckers and hooks.

sections.heading: 2. Taenia saginata — Beef tapeworm
paragraphs: Infection: ingestion of raw/undercooked beef containing Cysticercus bovis. Habitat: small intestine. Scolex: quadrate with four suckers; no rostellum and no hooks (unarmed scolex).
Gravid proglottid: uterus has numerous lateral branches, classically 12–30 (more than 12). Mature segments resemble those of T. solium, so the gravid segment is more useful for differentiation.
Taenia spp. eggs are morphologically indistinguishable from one another by routine microscopy. Do not identify T. solium versus T. saginata from the egg alone.
Cysticercus bovis is unarmed: its scolex has suckers but no rostellar hooks. This corrects a contradictory phrase in the supplied handout that mentions chitinized hooks under C. bovis.

sections.heading: 3. H. nana — Dwarf tapeworm
paragraphs: Egg: oval, with outer hyaline shell and inner embryophore; polar thickenings give rise to polar filaments; contains a hexacanth embryo (six hooklets). Polar filaments are the key practical clue.
Scolex: globular, four suckers, retractile rostellum with a single row of small hooks.
Mature proglottid: broad segment, bilobed ovary and three rounded testes; lateral genital pore. Gravid proglottid is filled with eggs.
Remember: H. nana egg = polar filaments; Taenia egg = radially striated shell and six hooklets but no polar filaments.
CDC image note: H. nana egg is approximately 30–50 µm and has 4–8 polar filaments between the membranes; the six-hooked oncosphere is inside.

sections.heading: 4. Diphyllobothrium latum — Broad fish tapeworm
paragraphs: Practical structures specified in the course: scolex with two longitudinal sucking grooves called bothria, and an operculated egg.
The egg is oval and operculated; the scolex is elongated rather than globular and bears bothria, not four cup-shaped suckers.
Identification key: operculated egg + bothria → Diphyllobothrium latum.
Terminology note: CDC now uses Dibothriocephalus latus (= Diphyllobothrium latum) in its updated nomenclature; the course name remains recognizable for the practical exam.

sections.heading: 5. Echinococcus granulosus — Hydatid cyst
paragraphs: Adult worm: very small cestode with scolex bearing an armed rostellum (double row of hooks) and usually three segments: immature, mature and a large terminal gravid segment.
Hydatid cyst wall has three layers: pericyst (outer host-derived fibrous layer), ectocyst (laminated acellular layer), and endocyst (inner germinal layer).
The germinal layer forms brood capsules and protoscolices. Protoscolex shows an invaginated scolex with four suckers and a double crown of hooklets.
Spotter words: Hydatid cyst, pericyst, ectocyst, endocyst, brood capsule, protoscolices.

sections.heading: 6. High-yield cestode distinctions
paragraphs: T. solium: armed scolex + pork-associated intestinal taeniasis + 7–13 uterine branches. T. saginata: unarmed scolex + beef + 12–30 branches; the ranges overlap at 12–13.
Taenia egg: spherical, radially striated embryophore, six-hooked embryo; species cannot be distinguished by egg morphology.
H. nana: polar filaments + retractile armed rostellum. D. latum: bothria + operculated egg. E. granulosus: hydatid cyst with three layers and protoscolices.
Exam trap: Taenia solium eggs can cause cysticercosis; do not equate pork-meat cysticercus ingestion with egg ingestion.

title: الديدان المثقوبة — Trematoda Diagnostic Atlas
subtitle: Fasciola hepatica • Schistosoma mansoni • S. haematobium • Heterophyes heterophyes
author: UMEDT — Parasitology Practical Course

sections.heading: 1. Fasciola hepatica — Liver fluke
paragraphs: Adult morphology: large, leaf-shaped, dorsoventrally flattened worm with highly branched intestinal caeca; testes are branched and arranged in tandem; ovary lies to the right of the midline; uterus is coiled anteriorly.
Habitat: bile ducts. Egg: large, oval/ellipsoidal and operculated, approximately 130–150 × 60–90 µm; passed unembryonated in stool.
Infective stage: metacercaria encysted on aquatic vegetation; infection follows ingestion of contaminated water plants such as watercress. The snail is an intermediate host.
Spotter: leaf-like adult + large operculated egg → Fasciola hepatica.

sections.heading: 2. Schistosoma — Blood flukes
paragraphs: Unlike most trematodes, Schistosoma are dioecious: male and female worms are separate. The male is shorter and broader; the female is longer and slender, residing in the gynecophoral canal of the male.
Infective stage: fork-tailed cercaria penetrates intact skin in freshwater. Diagnostic stage: eggs in stool or urine, depending on species.
S. mansoni egg: oval with a prominent lateral spine; typically found in stool. S. haematobium egg: oval with a terminal spine; classically found in urine.

Adult S. haematobium male in the supplied course images: about 1–1.5 cm, coarse tubercles on the tegument and approximately 3–5 testes; female about 2–2.5 cm with ovary in the posterior third. Retain the course's image labels for the practical spotter.

sections.heading: 3. Heterophyes heterophyes
paragraphs: Adult worm: small, pyriform (pear-shaped), with a broad rounded posterior part.
Egg: small, oval, operculated, with a small knob at the posterior end (abopercular knob).
Metacercaria is another practical stage shown in the supplied guide. If the image shows a pear-shaped adult or an operculated egg with a posterior knob, identify Heterophyes heterophyes.
Do not confuse its posterior knob with the prominent spine of Schistosoma eggs.

sections.heading: 4. Trematode image-recognition summary
paragraphs: Fasciola: leaf-like adult; branched internal organs; large operculated egg.
S. mansoni: oval egg + lateral spine + stool specimen. S. haematobium: oval egg + terminal spine + urine specimen.
Heterophyes: pyriform adult; small operculated egg + posterior knob; metacercaria.
Most trematodes are hermaphroditic; Schistosoma is the key exception with separate sexes.

title: مفتاح التعرف على صور العملي — Practical Spotter & Differential Diagnosis
subtitle: Eggs • Scoleces • Proglottids • Larvae • Adult Worms
author: UMEDT — Parasitology Practical Course

sections.heading: 1. Egg identification — ابدأ بالعلامة الفارقة
paragraphs: Mammillated thick shell → Ascaris fertilized egg. Elongated granular egg → Ascaris unfertilized egg.
Barrel-shaped egg with bipolar plugs → Trichuris trichiura. D-shaped / planoconvex egg → Enterobius vermicularis.
Rhabditiform larva with visible esophagus → Strongyloides stercoralis. Sheathed microfilaria with nuclei to tail tip → Loa loa.
Radially striated spherical egg with six hooklets → Taenia spp. (egg cannot distinguish T. solium from T. saginata). Oval egg with polar filaments → Hymenolepis nana.
Operculated egg: large → Fasciola hepatica or other large fluke eggs; small oval with posterior knob → Heterophyes. Schistosoma mansoni = lateral spine; S. haematobium = terminal spine.
Visual drill: identify the six images attached to this topic without reading their captions. For each one, state the organism, stage, specimen, and single diagnostic feature.

sections.heading: 2. Scolex and proglottid identification
paragraphs: Armed scolex (rostellum + two rows of hooks) → T. solium. Unarmed scolex with four suckers and no rostellum → T. saginata.
H. nana: globular scolex, four suckers, retractile rostellum with one row of small hooks.
D. latum: scolex with two bothria (longitudinal grooves), not four cup-shaped suckers.
T. solium gravid proglottid: usually 7–13 uterine branches. T. saginata: 12–30 branches. Count primary lateral uterine branches, not secondary subdivisions.

sections.heading: 3. The 10-second specimen algorithm
paragraphs: Step 1 — Determine specimen: stool, urine, blood film, tissue, or adult worm. Step 2 — Determine broad group: nematode, cestode, trematode. Step 3 — Find the unique structure: plugs, spine, operculum, polar filaments, rostellum, bothria, uterine branches, or larval esophagus.
Step 4 — Say the complete identification: organism + stage + one diagnostic feature. Example: “Schistosoma mansoni egg — oval with a prominent lateral spine.”
Step 5 — If the image is a Taenia egg, answer Taenia spp. only; do not guess the species from an indistinguishable egg.

sections.heading: 4. Corrections and exam cautions
paragraphs: Taenia solium uterine branches: CDC reference gives 7–13; T. saginata gives 12–30. This is more precise than the simple <12 / >12 shorthand.
Cysticercus bovis of T. saginata is unarmed; do not label it as having rostellar hooks. Cysticercus cellulosae of T. solium is armed.
Schistosoma mansoni has a lateral spine; S. haematobium has a terminal spine. Both are oval eggs, so spine position and specimen source are the differentiators.

The supplied course guide is the exam scope. When a course-sheet detail conflicts with a verified reference or appears internally inconsistent, the topic flags the discrepancy rather than silently teaching the error.

title: خطة مذاكرة الطفيليات العملية في يوم واحد — One-Day Master Plan
subtitle: 8-Hour Focused Revision • Active Recall • Image Spotters
author: UMEDT — Parasitology Practical Course

sections.heading: 1. جدول اليوم — 8 ساعات دراسة صافية تقريباً
paragraphs: Block 1 — 35 min: General concepts, routes of transmission and Helminths classification. أغلق الموضوع واكتب التعريفات والتصنيف من الذاكرة.
Block 2 — 90 min: Intestinal nematodes: Ascaris, Trichuris, Enterobius, Strongyloides. خصص 35 دقيقة للصور والبيض واليرقات، و55 دقيقة للفهم والاسترجاع.
Break — 15 min.
Block 3 — 85 min: Cestodes: Taenia solium, T. saginata, H. nana, D. latum, Echinococcus. ارسم السكلِكس وقارن gravid proglottids.
Break — 20 min.
Block 4 — 70 min: Trematodes: Fasciola, S. mansoni, S. haematobium, Heterophyes. ركز على شكل البيضة ومكان spine.
Block 5 — 30 min: Loa loa + vectors + infective versus diagnostic stages.
Block 6 — 50 min: Image spotter drill. افتح الصور، أخفِ captions، وسمّ organism/stage/key feature خلال 10–15 ثانية.
Block 7 — 35 min: MCQ and final correction. أجب عن اختبار الوحدة الثامنة ثم راجع الأخطاء فقط.
Total focused study: about 6 hours 35 minutes, plus 35 minutes of breaks. If you have a full day, use the remaining time for a second image-only round and sleep adequately.

sections.heading: 2. طريقة المذاكرة داخل كل Topic
paragraphs: First pass (الفهم): اقرأ Habitat, Mode of infection, Diagnostic stage and morphology. لا تحفظ العلاج قبل أن تتقن التعرف على العينة.
Second pass (الاسترجاع): أخفِ الإجابة واسأل نفسك: What is the infective stage? What specimen? What is the distinguishing feature?
Third pass (visual): ادرس الصور والمجسمات، ثم سمّ الصورة دون قراءة caption.
Final pass (exam): اكتب إجابة نموذجية قصيرة باللغة الإنجليزية، ثم اشرح سببها بالعربية.

sections.heading: 3. قائمة التحقق قبل دخول العملي
paragraphs: □ أميز fertilized vs unfertilized Ascaris eggs. □ أعرف bipolar plugs في Trichuris. □ أتعرف على D-shaped Enterobius egg. □ أفرق Strongyloides rhabditiform عن filariform.
□ أفرق armed T. solium عن unarmed T. saginata. □ أحفظ Taenia uterine branches. □ أتعرف polar filaments في H. nana وbothria في D. latum. □ أشرح طبقات hydatid cyst.
□ أميز lateral spine عن terminal spine. □ أتعرف leaf-like Fasciola adult وoperculated egg. □ أتعرف pyriform Heterophyes وposterior knob. □ أتذكر Loa loa microfilaria في blood film وChrysops vector.
□ أجيب عن MCQs في Topic 08 وأستطيع شرح سبب استبعاد الخيارات الخاطئة.

sections.heading: 4. طريقة تقييم نفسك
paragraphs: لكل كائن امنح نفسك درجة من 0 إلى 3: (0) لا أعرفه، (1) أعرف الاسم فقط، (2) أعرف الاسم والعلامة الفارقة، (3) أستطيع ذكر habitat/transmission/diagnostic stage والمورفولوجيا.
أي عنصر درجته 0 أو 1 يعود إلى المراجعة فوراً. لا تستهلك وقتاً إضافياً على العناصر التي تتقنها.
هدف اليوم: تمييز صور كل الأطوار المدرجة في الدليل، لا التوسع في طفيليات غير موجودة في نطاق المقرر.

author: UMEDT — Parasitology Practical Course

sections.heading: طريقة الاختبار — Attempt before reading answers
paragraphs: غطِّ سطر Answer في كل سؤال، واختر الإجابة أولاً. امنح نفسك دقيقة لكل سؤال. بعد ذلك اقرأ التفسير وحدد سبب خطأ الخيارات الأخرى.
الدرجة المقترحة: 22 سؤالاً × 1 درجة. 19–22 ممتاز؛ 16–18 جيد؛ 12–15 يحتاج مراجعة؛ أقل من 12 أعد Topic 06 ثم الاختبار.

sections.heading: MCQ Bank — Core practical questions
paragraphs: Q01. The infective stage of Ascaris lumbricoides for humans is: A) Unfertilized egg  B) Embryonated egg  C) Rhabditiform larva  D) Adult worm. Answer: B — الإنسان يبتلع embryonated egg.
Q02. The most characteristic egg feature of Trichuris trichiura is: A) Lateral spine  B) Polar filaments  C) Bipolar plugs  D) Operculum. Answer: C — barrel-shaped egg with two polar plugs.

Q03. The best routine diagnostic test for Enterobius vermicularis is: A) Blood film  B) Perianal cellophane-tape test  C) Urine microscopy  D) Sputum microscopy. Answer: B — eggs are deposited on perianal folds, especially at night.

Q04. Which Strongyloides stage is usually found in stool? A) Filariform L3  B) Rhabditiform larva  C) Microfilaria  D) Cysticercus. Answer: B — rhabditiform larvae are the usual diagnostic stage in stool.
Q05. Which Strongyloides stage penetrates human skin? A) Rhabditiform L1  B) Filariform L3  C) Egg  D) Adult female. Answer: B — infective filariform L3.
Q06. Loa loa is transmitted by: A) Anopheles  B) Chrysops  C) Culex  D) Biomphalaria. Answer: B — Chrysops day-biting fly.

Q07. The key blood-film clue for Loa loa microfilaria is: A) No sheath  B) Nuclei stop before tail tip  C) Nuclei extend to tail tip  D) Terminal spine. Answer: C — sheathed microfilaria with nuclei reaching the tip.
Q08. Taenia solium scolex is: A) Unarmed with bothria  B) Armed rostellum with two rows of hooks  C) Four suckers only  D) No suckers. Answer: B — armed rostellum and four suckers.
Q09. Taenia saginata scolex is: A) Armed  B) Unarmed, four suckers, no rostellum  C) Two bothria  D) Retractile rostellum. Answer: B — unarmed scolex.
Q10. Taenia spp. eggs can distinguish T. solium from T. saginata: A) True  B) False. Answer: B — eggs are morphologically indistinguishable; use scolex or gravid proglottid.
Q11. T. saginata infection is acquired by ingestion of: A) Pork cysticerci  B) Beef cysticerci  C) Embryonated eggs in water  D) Cercariae. Answer: B — Cysticercus bovis in undercooked beef.
Q12. The hallmark egg feature of Hymenolepis nana is: A) Bipolar plugs  B) Polar filaments  C) Terminal spine  D) Operculum. Answer: B — polar filaments between the membranes.
Q13. Diphyllobothrium latum scolex bears: A) Four cup-shaped suckers  B) Two bothria  C) Armed rostellum  D) One terminal spine. Answer: B — two longitudinal sucking grooves (bothria).
Q14. Hydatid cyst wall is classically described as: A) Two layers  B) Three layers  C) One layer  D) Four layers. Answer: B — pericyst, ectocyst and endocyst.
Q15. Fasciola hepatica adult is typically: A) Pear-shaped  B) Leaf-shaped  C) Cylindrical with curved tail  D) Segmented. Answer: B — leaf-like fluke with branched internal organs.
Q16. Schistosoma mansoni egg has: A) Terminal spine  B) Lateral spine  C) Polar filaments  D) Operculum. Answer: B — prominent lateral spine; usually stool specimen.
Q17. Schistosoma haematobium egg has: A) Lateral spine  B) Terminal spine  C) Bipolar plugs  D) Posterior knob only. Answer: B — terminal spine; classically urine specimen.

Q18. Which trematode is dioecious (separate sexes)? A) Fasciola  B) Heterophyes  C) Schistosoma  D) All trematodes. Answer: C — Schistosoma is the key exception to the usual hermaphroditic trematodes.

Q19. Heterophyes heterophyes egg is: A) Large with terminal spine  B) Small, operculated, with posterior knob  C) Barrel-shaped with plugs  D) Spherical and radially striated. Answer: B — posterior abopercular knob.
Q20. The infective stage of Schistosoma for humans is: A) Egg  B) Miracidium  C) Cercaria  D) Sporocyst. Answer: C — fork-tailed cercaria penetrates intact skin in freshwater.

Q21. Which is a correct pair? A) S. mansoni—urine  B) S. haematobium—stool only  C) S. mansoni—lateral spine  D) Fasciola—terminal spine. Answer: C — S. mansoni egg has a lateral spine and is classically found in stool.

Q22. Which pair correctly matches infective and diagnostic stages? A) Strongyloides: rhabditiform infective / filariform diagnostic  B) Strongyloides: filariform infective / rhabditiform diagnostic  C) Ascaris: unfertilized egg infective  D) Schistosoma: egg infective to human. Answer: B — L3 penetrates skin; rhabditiform larva is commonly detected in stool.

sections.heading: Rapid Viva — Answer aloud in English
paragraphs: Identify the egg with two bipolar plugs and state its infective route.
Differentiate the infective and diagnostic larval stages of Strongyloides stercoralis.
Why can a Taenia egg not distinguish T. solium from T. saginata?
Name the three layers of a hydatid cyst.
Differentiate S. mansoni and S. haematobium eggs by spine position and specimen.
State the vector and diagnostic specimen for Loa loa.

sections.heading: Final answer format — Model response
paragraphs: “This is an egg/larva/adult of [organism]. The diagnostic feature is [distinctive morphology]. The usual specimen is [stool/urine/blood/tissue].”
مثال: “This is a Schistosoma mansoni egg. It is oval with a prominent lateral spine and is usually identified in stool.”
